3854ad25f9a958ed.en_html: I first learned about IDFC in September of my first year at university. At a social gathering for university scholarship recipients, Hashimoto, an older student from my high school and the founder of IDFC, introduced it to me. Through high school, I had devoted myself to tennis with the goal of competing in the national inter-high school championships, but unfortunately I was unable to achieve that dream. Feeling that I had reached my limit as a player, I was constantly searching, after entering university, for something new into which I could pour my passion. Until then, I had really done nothing but tennis (laughs), so I had energy to spare. I wanted to keep broadening my horizons, and I thought I would use the agility I was proud of to try anything. 6ccfc58a3e247628.en_html: The reasons the university president explained revealed a history of Myanmar that went beyond anything I had imagined. Under the former military regime, university students were at the center of calls for democratization in Myanmar. Fearing that students would unite for democratization, the government reportedly closed universities in city centers and restricted student gatherings even at universities in the suburbs. Under those conditions, student organizations interacting with students from overseas could never have been permitted. I was convinced that it was highly significant for university students from Japan and Myanmar to build relationships ahead of other countries, without missing this moment when democratization had begun, and I started working toward establishing IDFC.

8a3b97ed54cfe939.en_html: In the course of these developments, I feel that we need to ask again why IDFC exists. I think a clue lies in the fact that it is an exchange between “Myanmar and Japan.” For example, if Japan is the first point of contact for Myanmar students, some connection to Japan will stay with them, and I think they may continue to engage with Japan in some way in the future. I am sure the same can be said of Japanese students. I think creating these seeds of exchange between Japan and Myanmar may be one of the roles that IDFC is uniquely able to fulfill.
